Step calibration, %1$s counter ticks per step

Counter ticks per step. Leave at 1.0 unless your steps run high. On a WHOOP 5/MG they can run very high (10× or more), so this goes up to 30. Walk a known 1,000 steps and divide NOOP\'s count by the real count to get your value.
Steps estimate calibration. %1$s. Opens the calibration screen.
For a WHOOP 4.0, which sends no step count: NOOP estimates steps from motion, calibrated to your phone. Tap to see how close it is and adjust it.
Choose how distances, weights, heights, temperatures and Effort are shown. Your data is always stored the same way. This only changes the display.
The language NOOP\'s own screens are shown in. Your data, units and metric names are unaffected. Screens not yet translated stay in English.
NOOP estimates your steps from your WHOOP\'s motion, calibrated to your phone\'s step count. It\'s an estimate, not a step counter. A WHOOP 4.0 doesn\'t transmit steps.
On the days your phone also counted steps, NOOP learns how much your motion maps to steps, then applies that to the strap-only days. The more matching days it has, the more it trusts the estimate.
We\'re not seeing any motion from your strap yet. Steps are estimated from your WHOOP\'s banked motion history, so your strap needs to sync that history before NOOP has anything to count.

Open NOOP near your strap and let it catch up (a full history sync can take a while on first run). Once a day or two of motion lands, your step estimate and the calibration below will start to fill in.
These are the days where your phone also counted steps, so NOOP can learn how your motion maps to steps. Or set the coefficient manually below.
No days yet where both NOOP and your phone counted steps. Once your phone logs a few days alongside the strap, they\'ll appear here so you can see how close the estimate is.
%1$s: estimated %2$d steps, phone %3$d steps, %4$d percent difference
These days are excluded from the estimate (your phone\'s real count is shown instead). They\'re here only so you can judge the estimate\'s accuracy.

Override the automatic fit with your own steps-per-motion value. Useful if your phone has no step history to learn from, or the estimate runs consistently high or low. Step all the way down to return to auto.
Manual steps coefficient, %1$s steps per motion unit
Takes effect on the next analytics pass (after the next sync).
Charge, effort and rest - scored with the model, explained in plain terms.
You\'ll likely wake around %1$d ± %2$d Charge if you sleep about %3$s tonight.
Estimate from today\'s effort, your typical sleep and your %1$d-night recovery baseline - not a measurement. Your real Charge is scored from tomorrow\'s HRV when you wake.

Charge weighs your heart-rate variability against your personal baseline (~55%%), resting heart rate (~20%%), rest quality (~15%%), respiration (~5%%) and skin-temperature deviation (~5%%). Effort is a 0 - %1$s cardiovascular load from time spent in each heart-rate zone. Rest is staged from movement and heart rate. The full on-device recompute from the strap\'s raw streams is a later port; the scores below are read from each day\'s cached metrics.

No scored days yet. Sync your strap to collect raw streams. Effort and Rest are scored once a day\'s data is in. Charge needs about four nights of sleep to learn your baseline (you\'ll see \"Calibrating\" until then), and keeps sharpening over your first couple of weeks. On a WHOOP 5 or MG the strap banks little history, so that night count can climb slowly or sit at 0 of 4 until you have worn it across a few nights. That\'s its sync limit, not a fault. Import your WHOOP export to skip the wait.
